questions: For the condition f(S_i / S_{i+1}) = A_i, is the fraction S_i / S_{i+1} required to be in simplest terms before applying f, or does f automatically reduce it to coprime P and Q as part of its definition?

When computing f(S_i / S_{i+1}), should we treat S_i and S_{i+1} as given (potentially not coprime) and reduce the fraction to simplest terms, or directly take P = S_i / g, Q = S_{i+1} / g where g = gcd(S_i, S_{i+1})?
Are the sequences S considered ordered tuples, meaning (S_1, S_2, ..., S_N) and a permutation of it are distinct if they satisfy the conditions, or are we only counting distinct multisets?
Is the gcd condition gcd(S_1, S_2, ..., S_N) = 1 applied to the entire sequence, meaning the greatest common divisor of all elements must be 1, or does it mean pairwise coprime?
For the score defined as the product of all elements, is the product taken over all S_i, i.e., S_1 * S_2 * ... * S_N?
Should the sum of scores be computed modulo 998244353 after summing all scores, or should each score be reduced modulo 998244353 before summation?
Are the elements S_i required to be positive integers, and if so, is there an upper bound on their values?
Is the sequence A guaranteed to be such that at least one good sequence exists, or could there be cases with zero good sequences, and if so, should the sum be 0?
